item: resume_after_exclusive_operation's retry loop is a function of its own, called from inside the try whose finally gives the exclusive window back (R163)
refs: R163; hunk pair from Q; PR #1429
summary: runner.resume_after_exclusive_operation is reached on the main thread by scripts/run_scale_bench.py, and its finally hands the scheduler's exclusive window back; CPython 3.13 leaves a for loop's back-edge outside the exception table of the try around it, so an interrupt delivered there would skip the release. The loop moved verbatim into _start_or_stand_down(retries, retry_delay) -> bool, called from inside the try, with no handler in it. Q wrote the pair; here the code and its new test file go in one commit. The dis test (Q's _uncovered_back_edges helper) is red with the old loop restored; the behaviour test (starts on the third try, the kill switch wins without starting, the retries run out and the watcher starts, each releasing the window once) is green on old and new code, so it pins that the move changed nothing. Needs tests/test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py from #1416.
